ledger.event: F34 landed as a control-plane records commit, not a writer envelope. AGENTS section 8 has the control plane write documentation directly, section 3 gives a records envelope no review, and T53 makes an archive-at-80-per-cent cut a records commit that does not issue a writer. A voluntary review ran anyway, because the commit edits the constitution, and it found the blocking defect described below. Three changes. AGENTS section 3 carries D-53's orchestration model: order follows the dependency the board states rather than the issuer's judgement, siblings run only on holds proved disjoint at the files and written down with a free slot not counting as proof, review slots are reserved so a returned lane never waits, and a seat census is read from the process table with a dead seat resumed on its own session id. The provisional group of D-49 moved to factory/OPERATING_MODEL.md under a table naming what enforces each bullet, checked at the objects: eight of the nine rows name a trap in the digest every packet carries, and the ninth, a writer never fast-forwards main, is already AGENTS section 3's push the branch only, never main. A duplicate moved, not a law. Section 9's index kept the rows a seat or an issuing control plane reaches for constantly and the rest moved verbatim, thirty-seven rows byte-identical. The review caught the control plane writing a rule with no object into the file every seat reads: the first draft said a lane carries a wave and a depends-on and order is derived from that graph, while no lane carries either field, nothing renders them and nothing checks them. That is D-54's own charge, a rule with no check is a diary, committed into the constitution by the session that had just read D-54. The sentence now states what the board supports and names F37 as the lane that would derive order from a field. It also caught One review slot as a threshold no dated row carries, against AGENTS section 6, and three numbers in this row that did not reproduce, which is why the sizes here are a command rather than digits: node factory/tools/sizeBudget.mjs prints AGENTS.md at 86.6 per cent of its 12 KB cap against 96.8 before, and the control-plane packet out of the band. The seat-packet and control-plane figures move when this row is written, so they are not pasted here (T04). factory/COPY.md pointed a child at a part of section 5 that moved and was corrected. factory/OPERATING_MODEL.md gained a 16 KB cap: a file that receives what a capped file sheds while being unmeasured itself is T01.

seatPacketKb returned to 26 by D-57, and F36 narrowed by D-58, both before F36 was issued rather than after it failed. D-56 raised the cap to 27 under protest and named the condition for the pressure coming off, F36 bringing the packet under 26; F34 did it by another route, so node factory/tools/packet.mjs cost now prints the seat packet at 25.3 KB and the band prints 97.4 per cent of 26. Leaving the cap at 27 would have kept a concession whose reason had expired. F36's method also collided with F31: a per-lane traps digest makes the bytes before the envelope differ by lane, which is the assertion X01 was reverted for nearly switching off, and it would silently retire the proof F34 rested on, that every provisional bullet is enforced by a trap in the digest every packet carries. So F36 keeps the half that is safe and still changes the slope, a trap naming its object plus compressing the traps that already name a check, and per-lane scoping is deferred with a trigger rather than dropped: the seat packet reaching 90 per cent again with no duplicate left to shed.

F36 issued at base 2c1159c, alone, narrowed by D-58. Three things: every trap gains an object naming the file or glob it binds to or a star meaning it binds everywhere; packet.mjs --self-test asserts every trap has one and that every non-star object resolves in the tree, so a trap pointing at a file that is not there fails the gate; and trapsDigest emits only the first sentence of a trap that already names a check, which is D-52's second remedy at about 2.7 KB and makes writing a check remove a trap's prose from every future packet. The envelope names what is NOT in scope and why, because the board's title still promises the deferred half. Envelope is 5877 bytes against a 6144 cap.

F36 returned at 5c8f2ce and the review says CORRECTIONS NEEDED, on the same defect for the third time in two lanes: an assertion satisfied by construction. The compression claim built its expected line by calling firstSentence and ruleNamesACheck, the same two functions trapsDigest calls to build the line being compared, so it pinned a ternary and nothing else; the reviewer gutted compression twice with one-line mutations and the gate stayed green, once turning compression off entirely at 12261 bytes and once truncating all seventy-one rows to 6923. The object-resolves claim had no vacuity guard where its sibling did, so setting every object to star made it vanish silently. The lane's substance is good and confirmed at the objects: 71 objects with 19 non-star all resolving and 52 star rows judged honest against their rule text, no stored rule edited, no digest row dropped, and F31's prefix byte-identical across two lanes with the envelope still last, which is what D-58 deferred the scoping half to protect. Correction 1 issued, narrower than the first envelope: traps.yaml is finished and withheld, and the correction may not write an assertion in terms of the functions that produce what it asserts.

F36 landed from writer/F36 at b106bd2, fast-forward, after one correction. Every trap carries an object: 52 are a star meaning it binds everywhere, 19 name a path, and node factory/tools/packet.mjs --self-test fails when a trap has no object, when a non-star object does not resolve in the tree, and when no trap carries a non-star object at all. trapsDigest emits only the first sentence of a trap whose stored rule names a check, and the stored rule keeps every sentence it had: traps.yaml took 71 insertions and 0 deletions. Measured at the objects: seat packet 25.3 to 23.6 KB, 90.9 per cent of the 26 KB cap D-57 restored, and the traps digest 12.0 to 10.3 KB. Digest to digest the compression removed 1702 bytes against D-52's estimate of about 2.7 KB, and the lane log carries both rather than adopting the estimate. F31 survives untouched, which is what D-58 deferred the scoping half to protect: the envelope part is last and the bytes before it are byte-identical for two different lanes, checked directly rather than through the self-test that claims it.

D-59 recorded and the queue reordered off id order for a stated dependency, which is the rule AGENTS section 3 gained in F34. D-59 names what three lanes demonstrated: this tier writes checks that pin the implementation rather than the property, and such a check is invisible to the seat's self-test and to the gate by construction, because it is built from the thing it is meant to test. It adopts three responses and explicitly declines a tier change, on the evidence that deepseek-flash produced three landed lanes at roughly a fifth of a dollar each and took correction accurately whenever the envelope dictated instead of offering; the envelopes were underspecified, not the seat too cheap. The falsifier is stated: a fourth assertion satisfied by construction, on a dictating envelope that names its own mutation, makes that reading wrong. The reorder: F37 absorbs S13 and S16, which are both factory/tools/seat.mjs, and gains traps.yaml and a wider title; a new lane F39 takes S14 and S15, the cloud writer path. Both come before F35 and F38 because a spark must be absorbed or dropped before sitting 11 closes and neither can be absorbed until its check exists.

F37 issued at base ae28aa9, alone, and it is the first envelope written to D-59's rule: every acceptance item names the mutation that must turn its check red, and the return pastes that mutation going red, because a check this tier cannot break on purpose is not done. Four claims about launching a seat. The packet reaches a seat on stdin rather than as an argv string, which is S13, measured when a 33 KB packet killed F33's first launch before it read a byte. A writer key is read from the store that owns it in the same act as the launch, which is S16, measured when both keys answered 401 in an open shell and 200 in the User scope after a rotation that never reached the terminal. Holds are proved disjoint by a command rather than assumed from a free slot, which AGENTS section 3 has required since F34 with nothing implementing it. A seat census comes from the process table through an injected lister, so the claim is testable instead of shelling out unconditionally. The two traps that pay for the first two are written in this lane; absorbing S13 and S16 is the control plane's act at landing, because factory/sparks.json is not the seat's file. Envelope is 6029 bytes against a 6144 cap.

F37 landed from writer/F37 at 1e67ae8, fast-forward, approved on the first return with no correction, which is a first for this sitting and the first lane written to D-59's rule that every acceptance item names the mutation that must turn its check red. Four checks, each driven red by the control plane and again by the reviewer on faithful mutations: a recipe that hands the packet over as an argv string, a Windows line that takes the key from a bare env rather than the user store, a disjointReport whose overlap is always empty, and a census that ignores its injected lister. S13 absorbed as T72 and S16 as T73. The disjoint command earned itself immediately by reporting F37 and F39 overlapping on factory/traps.yaml, an overlap the control plane created when it booked F39 and would have hit had it run them as siblings; AGENTS has required holds proved disjoint since F34 with nothing implementing it. Two findings the control plane could not settle and the reviewer did, by running the objects rather than reasoning about them. The rewritten qwen recipe line -p - < packet.txt was suspected of being an invention; the reviewer read the installed CLI source and ran the literal line against an unreachable port, and stdin is prepended to the prompt so the form works and the suspicion was wrong. The census over-reports: the reviewer's own pip show aider-chat was listed as two running aider seats, caught live, now S17. Not covered, and flagged rather than guessed: the aider and opencode carrier lines, neither harness being installed.

F39 issued at base 9934c6c, alone, and it takes the last two open sparks that have lanes. Five claims about the GitHub writer Action, each naming the mutation that must turn its check red. It becomes opt-in and idle by default, gated on a repository variable, because today issuing any lane fires a headless cloud seat onto writer/<LANE>, the branch a local worktree may already hold; on F33 exactly that happened and a stale key stopped it rather than design, which is S14. It takes the router instead of hardcoding DashScope and its own model table, so the cloud seat can reach the native path D-51 made default, and the secret it counts becomes the secret the call passes, which is S15 and which today turns T55's loud skip into a loud failure. A missing secret exits 0 with a reason. And the packet reaches it on stdin rather than as an argv string, which is T72 in the cloud path, surviving only because the runner is Linux. factory/tools/route.mjs is handed to the lane for its duration and the envelope says so rather than doing it silently; the router's answer does not change, only a second caller gains the ability to ask it.

F39 returned at 512e86b: CORRECTIONS NEEDED, and the defect is a new variant of the one D-59 names. The self-test defends launchSpec, the plan, exhaustively through a dry-run fixture, and never reaches lines 182 to 194 where the real env object and the real spawnSync live, so that block is dead code to it. Four lines mutate green independently: the base URL, the key, the model id and the stdin carrier can each be replaced with a wrong literal and the self-test still prints ok. The control plane found two of them, both named by the envelope; the review found the other two by mutating the block rather than reading the plan, and named the single root cause rather than four findings. The lane log's self-check sentence, that the plan's fields and stdin bytes come from a real child run, is true of the dry-run print and false as a claim about the invocation that ships, which is the sentence that would have carried this past a review by narrative. The review also settled a question the control plane could not: the assertion that no envelope is live is now T09, a check that cannot pass, because AGENTS section 3 takes the gate archive before the envelope is deleted, so it is red at every landing of every lane; before the job-level guard its redness tracked a real hazard and the guard severed that. Correction 1 rescopes it to the property, watch is idle when no envelope is live, driven both directions against a fixture.

F39 landed from writer/F39 at b9cf594, fast-forward, after one correction. The GitHub writer Action is opt-in at job level, so an unset CLOUD_WRITER leaves it idle and issuing a lane can no longer fire a headless cloud seat onto a branch a local worktree holds; on F33 exactly that happened and a stale key stopped it rather than design. It asks route.mjs for the path, base, key name and provider id instead of hardcoding DashScope and its own map, the router's answer being byte-identical at base and HEAD with only a providerModel field added, and it counts the key its own call passes. A missing secret exits 0 with a reason naming the key and the path. The packet arrives on stdin. Five mutations were driven red by the control plane on the corrected branch, each with a property-level message: the child's OPENAI_BASE_URL, its OPENAI_API_KEY, its OPENAI_MODEL, an argv element carrying the packet, and watch printing idle while a lane is issued. S14 absorbed as T74 and S15 as T75, which empties every spark that had a lane. The T09 finding is the one worth carrying: the assertion that no envelope is live had been red at every landing of every lane, because AGENTS section 3 takes the gate archive before the envelope is deleted, and it is now a property driven both directions against a fixture. node factory/tools/landingGate.mjs prints GATE PASSED at 21 of 21 with an envelope live, which it has not done in this repository before.

F35 and F38 issued together at base ecf24e8, the first siblings of this sitting and the first pair proved disjoint by a command rather than by a free slot: node factory/tools/seat.mjs disjoint F35 F38 printed 2 and 2 holds, none shared, run before either envelope was written. AGENTS section 3 has required that proof since F34 and F37 built the tool that gives it. F35 makes the alumni scan open the TRAPS file it already detects, so a lesson a child wrote in prose stops reaching the parent only when a person reads it, which is T71; it must split rows that name a check from rows that do not, emit only the former as candidate intakes, and count the rest, because an intake without a check is refused and a refused intake is noise the owner learns to skip. F38 stops the factory believing a seat about which model wrote the lane: a seat echoes the envelope's Runtime stamp because it cannot see its own id, the harness meter records what actually answered, and recording a return now checks one against the other through the id map that owns the relation rather than by string equality, since deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4.1-flash are one model at two vendors while an unversioned DashScope id is a different price. F38 is the first lane this sitting to name a keystone: it is the spend-pasted-in-the-lane-log step of the dual-runtime loop, and it makes that step checkable rather than trusted.
